student_answer: In preemptive scheduling the OS can forcibly interrupt a running process for a higher-priority one or when a time quantum expires, as in Round Robin. student_answer: Preemptive: the OS interrupts processes based on priority or time quanta—e.g., Round Robin and SRTF. Non-preemptive: a process keeps the CPU until it yields—e.g., FCFS and non-preemptive SJF. Preemptive gives fairness; non-preemptive risks CPU monopoly by one process.
